subject: Private deployment: phase-in platform fee + surge capacity credit request
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@medicatech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment pricing questions (RFP follow-up)

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our procurement and infrastructure teams after reviewing the RFP (attached). Two asks stood out: 1) Can Redwood phase in the platform fee across the first 12 months (we're asking for 50% in Q1, 75% in Q2, 100% thereafter) given our pilot will be limited initially? 2) We anticipate occasional surge capacity events during model retraining and spikes — is there a one-time credit or burst allowance you can provide (we were thinking of 200 GPU-hours as a credit)?

Also, our CFO is sensitive to upfront fees; if we commit to a 36-month reserved capacity, what additional discount can you extend on top of the listed node pricing?

Attaching the RFP and a short procurement checklist.

Best,
Susan
Head of Cloud Ops
MedicaTech

Attachments: MedicaTech_RFP_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@medicatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions (RFP follow-up)

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the RFP. Quick response while I loop in finance and deals:

- Phase-in of platform fee: We can accommodate a 3-step phase-in similar to what you described for a pilot, but we'd like to align milestone triggers (pilot go-live, production onboarding, and first full-traffic month) rather than strict quarter boundaries. We'll propose schedule language in the term sheet.

- Surge (burst) credit: We can offer a 200 GPU-hour one-time credit for the pilot, or alternatively a smaller rolling buffer (e.g., 50 GPU-hours/month for 6 months). Which aligns better with your ops model?

- 36-month commit: We can add an additional 8–12% discount on top of node list pricing depending on committed minimums and prepay terms. Also open to combining with migration credits (one-time implementation credit) if you take the reserved pool.

I'll draft a term-sheet variant and send it by Wednesday. Marissa — can you confirm standard milestone definitions for the phase-in language? Ben — please surface the highest discount we can extend if they prepay 12 months up front.

Thanks,
Monica
Sr. Dir., Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Monica Patel
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions (RFP follow-up)

Monica / Ben — draft guidance below that we can use in the term sheet and for procurement: 

1) Phase-in schedule (milestone-driven)
   - Milestone A (Pilot activation): 50% platform fee for first 90 days after pilot go-live
   - Milestone B (Production onboarding): 75% platform fee for first 90 days after production ingress
   - Milestone C (Full traffic month): 100% thereafter
   - Milestone verification: mutually agreed runbook and smoke test results (attached example).

2) Surge credit options
   - Option 1 (one-time): 200 GPU-hour credit applied to first 6 months of invoices
   - Option 2 (buffered): 50 GPU-hours/month credit for 6 months (automatic carryover up to first 3 months)

3) Commit discounts
   - 36-month, prepaid 12 months up-front: additional 12% off node list
   - 36-month, quarterly prepaid: additional 9% off node list
   - Migration / implementation credit: up to $120k applied against first invoice if signed within 30 days

Note: we should avoid hard-coding exact SLA credits in the term sheet at this stage. Keep language contingent on SOW acceptance.

I'll assemble a variant term sheet (v1.3) combining these bullets and send to Monica for review.

Marissa
Principal Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: PhaseIn_Runbook_Example.docx

From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@medicatech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medicatech.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions (RFP follow-up)

Monica / Marissa — appreciate the quick turn. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The milestone approach works for us, but our security team will want the pilot verification checklist in writing. Can Marissa add the runbook as an appendix to the term sheet?

- For the surge credit, we prefer Option 1 (one-time 200 GPU-hours) because our training windows are bursty. If possible, we want the credit to apply before any overage billing during the first 6 months.

- On the 36-month commit: the CFO will not agree to prepay. Is there room to bump the quarterly-prepay discount to 11% if we add a 24-month guaranteed minimum consumption?

We'll review your term-sheet variant and come back with redlines.

Thanks,
Susan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@medicatech.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions (RFP follow-up)

Susan — quick note from commercial side. We can accept Option 1 for the surge credit and apply it before any overage billing in the first 6 months. On the discount: we can move the quarterly-prepay discount to 11% (from 9%) if MedicaTech agrees to a 24-month minimum committed consumption (X GPU-hours per month baseline, to be defined). We'll capture the baseline in the SOW and include an overage rate that steps down at higher volume tiers.

I'll have Marissa bake these edits into term-sheet v1.3 and send back with the pilot runbook appendix. If MedicaTech signs within 21 days, we can also add a $80k implementation credit on top of the migration credit.

Monica — flagging for renewal cadence discussions (we may want an annual usage review clause).

Best,
Ben
Head of Enterprise Deals
Redwood Inference

--
Redwood attachments to follow: Redwood_Private_Term_Sheet_v1.3.xlsx
